# Paneflow on Windows

> Install Paneflow on Windows with the signed MSI. Verify the installation, fix command lookup, and choose the Linux build for WSL2.

Canonical: https://paneflow.dev/docs/installation/windows

<!-- Auto-generated mirror of paneflow.dev - do not edit by hand.
     Source of truth: the paneflow.dev docs. Regenerated by
     scripts/sync-public-docs.ts in the site repo. -->

Paneflow runs natively on **Windows 10 version 1809 or later** and
**Windows 11**, on **x86_64 (Intel or AMD)**. Install the MSI for Windows
projects. If your repositories and agents are in a Linux distribution,
see the WSL2 section below.

## Install Paneflow with the MSI

1. Open the [Paneflow download page](/download) or the
   [latest Paneflow release on GitHub](https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/releases/latest).
2. Download `paneflow-0.17.6-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.msi`.
3. Verify the file's signature as described below, then run the MSI.
   Approve the Windows administrator prompt to continue.
4. Keep **PATH Environment Variable** selected to use `paneflow` from a
   terminal. The default install folder is `%ProgramFiles%\PaneFlow`.
5. Finish the installation, then open **PaneFlow** from the Start menu.

You do not need Rust or build tools. Install your CLI agents separately,
then follow the [getting started guide](/docs) to open a project and run an agent.

## Verify the MSI signature

In PowerShell, open the folder containing the downloaded MSI and run:

```powershell
$version = "0.17.6"
$signature = Get-AuthenticodeSignature ".\paneflow-$version-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.msi"
$signature.Status
$signature.SignerCertificate.Subject
```

The status should be `Valid`, and the certificate subject should identify
**Strivex** as the publisher. If the file is missing, check the folder and
filename. If the signature is invalid or the publisher differs, download
a fresh copy from the release page before proceeding.

SmartScreen can still show a reputation warning for a signed file. Check
the signature and publisher first. If a managed PC blocks installation,
ask its administrator.

## Verify the installation

Open a new PowerShell window and run:

```powershell
paneflow --version
```

The command should print the installed version. Also check that the app
opens from the Start menu.

If `paneflow` is not recognized, close all terminal windows and reopen
PowerShell from the Start menu. If it is still unavailable, try the default
install path:

```powershell
& "$env:ProgramFiles\PaneFlow\paneflow.exe" --version
```

If you chose another folder, use that path instead. If the full path works,
use it while you rerun the MSI to restore **PATH Environment Variable**.
If the executable is missing, check the install folder or reinstall.

New panes use the shell selected in Paneflow's **Settings**. Without a
configured shell, Paneflow tries PowerShell 7, Windows PowerShell,
`%ComSpec%`, then `cmd.exe`.

## Windows versions and requirements

| Environment | Availability | Requirements |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 11 x86_64 | Native MSI | A working GPU driver with DirectX 11 feature level 10 or later. |
| Windows 10 1809+ x86_64 | Native MSI | The same graphics requirements. |
| Windows before 10 1809 | Unsupported | Upgrade Windows before installing. |
| Windows ARM64 | No ARM64 MSI | The Windows release provides an x86_64 installer only. |
| WSL2 with WSLg | Linux build | Windows 10 build 19044+ or Windows 11, plus a compatible GPU driver. |

## Native Windows or WSL2?

Use the native app for Windows files, shells, and agents. Launch it from
the Start menu or a Windows shell, including when you use WSL inside a pane.

Use the Linux build inside WSL2 when your repositories, agents, and tools
are installed in Linux. WSLg displays the Linux app's window. Set up WSL2
and GUI support with [Microsoft's WSLg instructions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/tutorials/gui-apps),
then follow the [Linux installation guide](/docs/installation/linux)
from your Linux terminal. Choose the package for your distribution and
architecture. WSL1 cannot display Linux GUI apps through WSLg.

## Known Windows caveats

- Prefer PowerShell or Git Bash to `cmd.exe` for tracking a pane's current
  directory. `cmd.exe` does not report directory changes through OSC 7.
- Remote Desktop, launches from WSL2 or dev containers, CJK input methods,
  and some `Ctrl+C` behavior can have Windows-specific limitations.
  If a problem persists on the latest release, [report a Windows issue](https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/issues)
  with the Paneflow version, Windows build, shell, and steps to reproduce.

## Terminal backend

Ghostty's `libghostty-vt` terminal engine is included in the Windows build.
You do not need to install it or choose a backend. An old `terminal.backend`
key in `paneflow.json` is ignored. Read [how Paneflow uses Ghostty on Windows](/blog/libghostty-windows)
for the migration history.

## Update and uninstall

Before upgrading, save files and finish active commands. The MSI can stop
running terminal sessions during an upgrade.

Use the in-app updater or download and run
[`paneflow-0.17.6-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.msi`](/download). If an update
reports a corrupt download, or restarts the same version, install the
latest MSI manually. This also applies to the known update failures in
0.7.7/0.7.8 and 0.17.0/0.17.1; you do not need to install an intermediate version.

Uninstall Paneflow from Windows Settings. This removes the installed app
but preserves `%USERPROFILE%\.paneflow`, including `paneflow.json`,
saved sessions, managed worktrees, and helper binaries under `bin`.
